88: To uproot their feet - from the platform; rather, they stand bent in front of the ark. One can learn from here the order of the Priestly Benediction: how [the priest] uproots his feet from his place during the [blessing of Temple] Service, and comes before the ark, and prays "May it be Your will, ... that this blessing etc." as was stated earlier [Sotah 39a:6]. He prolongs this [prayer] until the congregation's Amen to the [blessing of] Thanksgiving is finished. The prayer leader announces "Priests" if there are two of them; if there is [only] one, he does not make the announcement, and [the one priests] turns around of his own accord, in accordance with Abaye, who stated earlier, "when there is one [priest] he does not call: Priest" [Sotah 38a:15]. When the statement of the caller finishes, he recites the blessing "who has sanctified us etc." [Sotah 39a:5]. After that, they begin the benediction. When the congregation's final Amen finishes, [the priests] turn around and bend their joints if they wish. The prayer leader begins "Grant peace" and the priests pray "Master of the Universe, we have performed that which You decreed upon us etc." [Sotah 39a:6], and prolong it until the prayer leader finishes the blessing. They uproot their feet and go their own way.
